THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 26 November 1833 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — CORROBORATION, NOT A NEW FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's fourth annual reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, held 18 May 1882, printed this man among the guests present as “Peacock, Elijah, 98 State street, Chicago.” (Chicago Tribune, 19 May 1882). The club's criterion was residence in Chicago before 1 January 1840 and majority by then: the roster therefore corroborates a pre-1840 Chicago residence and says he was alive in 1882. It gives NO year of arrival, and the address it prints is where he lived in 1882, forty-seven years after the scene date — it is not an 1835 residence and is not read as one. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). THE 1840 FEDERAL CENSUS — A HEAD FIVE YEARS AFTER THE SCENE, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1840 federal census of Chicago, read line by line off the left sheets in this repository, carries 1 head of this name — “Elijah Peacock” (33S7-9YYJ-RC, printed page 217, line 19). This project has ruled the head a MATCH for this person: the full name agrees, it is unique on both sides, and a discriminator independent of the name — directory persistence — separately places the same person in Chicago after the 1840 book was taken. Under the rule that decided it (L6 matched), by the crosswalk's own ladder (data/research/census_1840/resident_crosswalk.json). LATER EVIDENCE ONLY. The ratified grading ladder binds: an 1839 or 1840 appearance alone is never an 1835 resident, and 1840 household composition is never back-projected to the 1835-07-01 scene. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and an 1840 head is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
